doc.title: Bill Goodwin interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 28, 2025

chapter: Gary Burton and the move east
title: Auditioning for Gary Burton on Falling Grace
summary: Steve Swallow recommended him; Roy Haynes was leaving; he flew east, played one tune and was hired.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: I’m here because — speaking of bass players — because of Steve Swallow. He just kept mentioning my name to Gary because Steve and I were friends and he said, “You know Bill Goodwin would really like to do this gig, he’s often said that to me.” So Gary called me up and says, “Swallow keeps mentioning that we’re looking for a new drummer. Roy Haynes is leaving the group, would you like to audition for the gig?” I said, “Yeah I would, man, it’d be great.” So he sends me a ticket and I fly back to New York and we go to his house on Long Island, Swallow comes out on the train and we play one tune, and the tune was “Falling Grace,” which I had never heard before in my life.
I’d never heard it. And so I played it and I guess they liked it ‘cause I played one tune on the audition and then we played another one for fun and I got hired.
That’s very interesting ‘cause I just listened to it this morning because I knew that was part of your story. And when I was listening to it —
How do you learn these things, Monk?
But I was listening to it thinking of how that was for you and I can imagine it was a challenge.
It was what it was supposed to be. You know to me it was like well I’m here and I’m going to get this gig you know.
